correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the completed cubic stability polynomial and all five graph-distance matrix entry types from exact Laplacian powers on trees. Adjacent entries are positive by a negative quadratic discriminant; diagonal cubics are strictly decreasing with one positive root; distance-two entries change sign at the degree-triple threshold. The convex-forward-Euler representation proves the universal bound and exact equality; comparing degree-maximum diagonal polynomials proves unique star extremality, while direct star entries establish attainability. An independent integer-arithmetic enumeration of 18,248 labeled trees through order seven checks every coefficient and the endpoint signs. Finite checking supplements rather than replaces the general proof.

originality.rationale: Seven semantic searches for method aliases, graph-Laplacian Taylor polynomials, sharp two-edge path certificates and star extremality yielded related but nonidentical published comparisons. The 16-page Horváth primary work and complete accessible primary studies of SSP Runge–Kutta and polyhedral invariant-step conditions were materially inspected. Those texts yield general sufficient bounds or abstract root criteria, but do not explicitly entail the all-tree exact graph-local classification, the strictness iff condition, or unique star maximality. Previously available own-ledger cubic-adjacent work concerned fourth-order Runge–Kutta on maximum-degree-two graphs or different rational methods. Residual risk from unindexed/inaccessible equivalent results remains, so independence and complete novelty certification are not claimed.
residual_risks: Relevant unindexed or inaccessible publications could contain an equivalent exact tree theorem; searches and accessible primary-text inspections do not prove absolute priority.

value.rationale: For positive tree-network diffusion, choosing a physically admissible third-order timestep is a natural practical and structural problem. This theorem converts a dense-matrix nonnegativity condition into O(n) local degree data and univariate roots, sharpens the common Euler-based sufficient timestep exactly when tree topology allows it, and settles natural fixed-maximum-degree extremal trees and the equality classification for every size/degree. The star-versus-saturated-three-hub distinction is an infinite structural separation, not a one-off parameter substitution or unmotivated small table. The proof and exact finite replay make these bounds reusable for graph-indexed diffusion solvers.
